name: Philip
overview: Philip was a male member of the tribe of Edom, known uniquely as the brother of Herod. He held the position of Tetrarch over the regions of Iturea and Trachonitis, indicating his rule over these territories. His role as a ruler is highlighted in the New Testament, situating him within the Herodian dynasty.
namesAndTitles: Philip is identified by the proper name 'Philip,' with no specific meaning provided in the biblical text. He also held the title 'Tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis,' which denotes his authority as a great prince over these lands, emphasizing his political and territorial leadership.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Philip as the brother of Herod and the husband of Herodias, connecting him closely to the Herodian family. These relationships are noted in Matthew 14:3 and provide insight into his familial and political alliances.
scriptureSignificance: Philip's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his leadership as tetrarch and his familial ties within the Herodian dynasty. His governance of Iturea and Trachonitis places him among the regional rulers during the time of John the Baptist and Jesus. His connection to Herod and Herodias also situates him within the complex political and social dynamics of the period.
